seo.title: Wet Room Installation in Sunningdale | Tanked, Level-Access Floors | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Fit-only wet room installation in Sunningdale. Tanked, level-access floors with a tested fall to drain, suited to large plots on private and gated roads. From £3,500.

hero.intro: Ask where a wet room's drain should sit and the honest answer, more often than not in Sunningdale, is wherever suits the room best — the large detached properties here, from Victorian and Edwardian houses to inter-war family homes and more recent executive-style builds, tend to sit on plot sizes generous enough to put real choice back on the table. Much of Sunningdale's housing sits on private or gated roads around the golf courses the village is known for, and that privacy comes with a practical bonus for a project like this: fewer shared boundaries and structural party-wall constraints to work around when a waste run needs repositioning. None of that removes the need to check it properly — a generous plot doesn't tell us joist depth or where the existing waste pipe actually runs, only the survey does — but it does mean the conversation at survey tends to be about what you want rather than what the building will allow.

sections.heading: What a wet room installation involves
sections.body: A wet room has no tray and no step — the whole floor becomes the shower, falling to a single drain point, which means the floor build-up, the fall and the tanking all have to be right before a tile is chosen. We strip back to the joists, assess how far the floor can drop or be built up, and install the drain and first-fix plumbing at the position giving the cleanest fall, typically 1:60 to 1:80, set out with a laser level and checked again once tiling begins. Tanking runs across the full floor and walls to shower height, flood-tested before any tile goes down, with large-format tiles then laid to the fall and checked for lippage row by row. A glass screen or half-height panel is fitted where specified, and the project finishes with a water test and a full snagging walkthrough before handover.

sections.heading: Repositioning a wet room drain in a Sunningdale property
sections.body: A generous Sunningdale plot — whether period or executive-style — tends to give us more freedom over where a drain or waste run actually sits than a terraced or semi-detached property would allow elsewhere. If the room layout would benefit from a linear channel running along one wall rather than a central point drain, that's usually achievable without being forced into whatever position the existing waste pipe dictates. The same freedom applies to widening a doorway for level access or moving a waste run three feet to suit a different fixture arrangement. We'll still check original joist depth carefully in an older Victorian or Edwardian Sunningdale house before committing to a floor build-up, since the freedom a large plot gives on layout doesn't change what a period timber floor can structurally take.

sections.heading: Booking your Sunningdale wet room survey
sections.body: Every wet room starts with the £125 survey, where we confirm joist depth, the achievable drain position, and the ceiling below if the room sits upstairs, before any quote is written. The programme then runs through floor build-up and first-fix plumbing, tanking and a flood test, tiling set out from the drain outward, and a final snagging stage with water run across the whole floor to confirm nothing pools. We fit only, working from the tiles, screen and sanitaryware you've sourced yourself, and the written scope separates the structural floor cost from the finishing specification. Book a survey to get a firm quote for your Sunningdale wet room.

faqs.q: Does living on a private or gated Sunningdale road affect how you schedule a wet room installation?
faqs.a: It mainly affects access arrangements rather than the work itself — we'll confirm any gate codes, parking restrictions or delivery windows at survey so materials and skip collections run smoothly, but the installation process is the same as anywhere else.

faqs.q: Can the wet room drain be repositioned to suit a new layout in my Sunningdale house?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The generous plot sizes typical of Sunningdale properties tend to give more freedom over drain position than a smaller or terraced property would, though the existing waste pipe route is still checked at survey before anything is confirmed.

faqs.q: Will an older Sunningdale property's floor joists take a wet room floor build-up?
faqs.a: Most can, but we check joist depth and condition at survey on every Victorian or Edwardian property before agreeing a floor build-up — plot size doesn't change what the existing timber floor can structurally support.

faqs.q: How much does a wet room installation cost in Sunningdale?
faqs.a: From £3,500, with the final figure depending on floor build-up required, tanking area and tile format — all confirmed in writing after the £125 survey, which is deducted from the project cost if you go ahead.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Sunningdale wet room installation page, showing a finished result rather than a work-in-progress. Subject and action: a completed wet room with a level floor in dark anthracite stone-effect tile falling toward a discreet linear channel drain set against one wall, no step or tray anywhere in the room. Setting and work-stage: a principal en-suite in a large executive-style Sunningdale house near the golf courses, finished and in everyday use, mid-morning. Composition: wide shot taken from the open doorway looking across the room toward a north-facing window, the linear drain and floor fall visible in the foreground, a brushed nickel shower valve mounted on the far wall. Light and materials: cool, bright midday daylight through a north-facing window giving a crisp, slightly blue-toned light, dark anthracite basalt-effect large-format porcelain floor and wall tiles, brushed nickel shower valve and towel radiator, light falling evenly but with a noticeably cooler cast than a south-facing room and soft natural shadow beneath the window reveal. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting under every shelf or mirror, no catalog-symmetrical staging or twin fixtures, no single uniform gold or amber colour wash across the frame, no plants, florals or candles as styling props, no shower shown running water, varied and believable surface sheen rather than uniform hyper-gloss.
image.heroAlt: Finished wet room with dark anthracite stone-effect tiled floor falling to a linear wall drain and brushed nickel fittings, in an executive-style Sunningdale house under cool daylight.
